- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently underreacts to recent price spikes; if last 3–5 days show sharp upward movement, increase forecast slightly to capture momentum.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.5 to -0.5), adjust forecast to reflect faster reversion than model suggests.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overextension.
- If sentiment history shows alternating extremes (e.g., +0.5 then -0.5), model may misalign with sentiment cycles; apply smoothing to avoid abrupt directional shifts.
